Hi Samira / Ben —

Thanks for the call last week. Per our handoff, attaching the initial onboarding checklist to capture the provisioning milestones and ownership for the dedicated GPU pool. High level asks from our side to get the activation sprint scheduled: 

- Confirm preferred primary region (us-west-2 or us-east-1) and acceptable secondary region for cross-region fallback.
- Baseline QPS / concurrency target (tokens/s or reqs/s) for peak traffic and expected production date range.
- Any limits for burst pre-warming (e.g., max nodes that NetOps can allow to warm).

Proposed next step: run a 2-hour burst simulation targeted at your top endpoint to validate autoscale/coordinator handoffs. I propose Wed Nov 17 14:00-16:00 PT or Thu Nov 18 09:00-11:00 PT — please confirm which window works for your SREs.

Key attachments: elara_onboard_checklist.xlsx (checkpoints + owner matrix).

Action items for Elara: confirm region choice and provide a point of contact for NetOps who can approve cross-region IP/firewall opening for the simulation.

I'll loop in Kimberly from Ops after you confirm the window so we can book the runbook review.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber

Thanks Jonas —

Appreciate the checklist. Quick answers:
- Primary region: us-west-2 (preferred). Secondary fallback: us-east-1.
- Peak target: ~120 concurrent requests (avg token length ~300) — we expect spikes up to 200 concurrent for short windows.
- NetOps pre-warm limit: we can allow up to 50 additional GPUs for a 30–60 minute warm window, but anything beyond requires exec approval.

We can support the Nov 17 window (14:00–16:00 PT). I'll schedule SRE and NetOps and add Ben for procurement coordination. Attaching our SRE constraints doc so you have the firewall & IP whitelist expectations.

Can you confirm the autoscale behavior you'll run during the simulation (warm pool size, burst multiplier, cooldown)?

Samira Patel
Head of Platform Ops | Elara Systems
samira.patel@elara.com | +1 (650) 555-4499

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, RackNorth Sales <sales@racknorth.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:23:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity onboarding: final ops checklist & regional fallback simulation

Samira — thanks, that works. Confirming Nov 17 14:00–16:00 PT for the burst sim. Below is the simulation plan we propose (short version):

- Warm baseline: maintain 30 GPUs warm (steady state for pre-warm).
- Burst policy: allow dynamic burst up to 200% of baseline (i.e., up to 60 GPUs) for 30 minutes, then step down with a 15-minute cooldown window.
- Autoscale triggers: scale-up on 90% CPU or 85% token latency SLA breach across 3 consecutive 15s windows. Scale-down after 15 minutes of under-threshold.
- Fallback behavior: if us-west capacity is exhausted or degraded, requests will fail-open to us-east (regional fallback) with traffic shifting gradually over 60s; KV cache warming will occur on first request.

Please note: RackNorth (cc'ed) will provide the reserved pool provisioning for this simulation and will need the final acceptance to provision burst capacity on their side.

Attachments: runbook-dedicated-pool-v1.pdf (runbook excerpt).

Next actions (owners):
- Elara NetOps: open firewall ranges listed in elara_sre_constraints.pdf (Samira)
- RackNorth: confirm provisioning window and quota (RackNorth Sales)
- Redwood Ops: validate autoscale triggers & warm pool orchestration (Kimberly / Rishi)
- Redwood CS: run the simulation and collect traces (Jonas)

If everyone is aligned I'll send a calendar invite and a final runbook a day before the sim.

Cheers,
Jonas
